children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a picture that shows that 9 can also be written as the difference of two squares.

answer.worked:
Draw a $5\times5$ counter array and distinguish the lower-left $4\times4$ square. The top row and rightmost column contain the nine remaining counters.

$\begin{align*}5^2-4^2&=25-16\\5^2-4^2&=9.\end{align*}$

spec.description: Five-by-five counter array with an orange top row and rightmost column, and a blue lower-left four-by-four square.
spec.mathematics: Twenty-five counters minus sixteen counters leaves nine.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Expand $(n+1)^2-n^2$, and then use this to prove that every odd number can be written as the difference of two squares.

answer.short:
$(n+1)^2-n^2=2n+1$.

Every odd number has the form $2n+1$ for some integer $n$, so it is the difference of these two squares.
answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}(n+1)^2-n^2&=n^2+2n+1-n^2\\(n+1)^2-n^2&=2n+1.\end{align*}$

Every odd number is $2n+1$ for some integer $n$. Hence every odd number can be written as $(n+1)^2-n^2$, the difference of two squares.
